literal: Li Yuanzhong; younger clansman Mi; clansman uncle Jingyi; Lu Wenwei; Sun Xunzu; clansman Yong; Li Yishen
idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong; his younger clansman Mi; his clansman uncle Jingyi; Lu Wenwei; Sun Xunzu; his clansman Yong; and Li Yishen

literal: Li Yuanzhong was a native of Bo in Zhao Commandery.
idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong came from Bo in Zhao Commandery.

literal: His great-grandfather Ling served in Wei as Governor of Ding Province and Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ling had served in Wei as governor of Ding Province and duke of Julu.

literal: His grandfather Hui was General Who Guards the West.
idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was general who guards the west.

literal: His father Xianfu was Governor of An Province.
idiomatic: His father Xianfu was governor of An Province.

literal: In youth Yuanzhong cultivated resolute integrity and was known for filial piety during mourning.
idiomatic: In youth Yuanzhong forged a resolute character and won renown for filial piety in mourning.

literal: He inherited the title Viscount of Pingji.
idiomatic: He inherited the title viscount of Pingji.

literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi of Wei became Minister of Works, he recruited Yuanzhong as staff officer in the personnel bureau.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi of Wei became minister of works, he recruited Yuanzhong as staff officer in the personnel bureau.

literal: When Yi was transferred to Grand Commandant, he again recommended him as senior itinerant staff officer.
idiomatic: When Yi was transferred to grand commandant, he again recommended him as senior itinerant staff officer.

literal: Later when Yi became Grand Tutor, he was soon ordered Grand Director-General for the Construction of the Bright Hall, and again took Yuanzhong as chief clerk.
idiomatic: Later, when Yi became grand tutor, he was soon ordered grand director-general for the construction of the Bright Hall and again took Yuanzhong as chief clerk.

literal: Yuanzhong had a rough knowledge of historical works and the arts of yin-yang and numerology; he could play the zither and drum, also loved archery and slingshot, and had ingenious ideas.
idiomatic: Yuanzhong had read widely in history and the arts of yin-yang and numerology. He could play the zither and drum, loved archery and slingshot, and had a gift for invention.

literal: When his mother died he left his post.
idiomatic: When his mother died he left his post.

literal: Before long, Governor of Xiang Province Prince of Anle Jian invited him to be commander in the princely household, but Yuanzhong, in deep mourning, firmly declined.
idiomatic: Before long, Governor of Xiang Province Prince of Anle Jian invited him to serve as commander in the princely household, but Yuanzhong, still in deep mourning, firmly declined.

literal: At first, because his mother was old and often ill, Yuanzhong devoted himself to medicine, studying for years until he became skilled in the healing arts.
idiomatic: At first, because his mother was old and often ill, Yuanzhong devoted himself to medicine. He studied for years until he mastered the healing arts.

literal: By nature he was benevolent and forgiving; whenever he saw the sick, regardless of rank, he treated them.
idiomatic: By nature he was benevolent and forgiving. Whenever he saw the sick, high or low, he treated them.

literal: The family had long been wealthy; household members in the countryside often made loans at interest, but Yuanzhong repeatedly burned the contracts and released debtors from obligation.
idiomatic: The family had long been wealthy. Household members in the countryside often made loans at interest, but Yuanzhong repeatedly burned the contracts and released the debtors.

literal: The people of the district greatly respected him.
idiomatic: The people of the district held him in deep respect.

literal: During Emperor Xiaoming of Wei's reign bandits rose everywhere; five hundred men from Qinghe who had been garrisoned in the west, returning through Southern Zhao Commandery, found the roads blocked and together sought refuge with Yuanzhong.
idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaoming of Wei's reign bandits rose everywhere. Five hundred men from Qinghe, returning from garrison duty in the west through Southern Zhao Commandery, found the roads blocked and together sought refuge with Yuanzhong.

literal: They presented a thousand bolts of silk; Yuanzhong accepted only one bolt, slaughtered five sheep to feed them, and sent a servant to guide them, saying, "If you meet bandits, simply say Li Yuanzhong sent you on your way.
idiomatic: They presented a thousand bolts of silk. Yuanzhong accepted only one, slaughtered five sheep to feed them, and sent a servant to guide them. "If you meet bandits," he said, "simply tell them Li Yuanzhong sent you on your way.

literal: " The servant did as told, and the bandits all let them pass.
idiomatic: " The servant did as he was told, and the bandits all let them pass.

literal: At the beginning of Yongan he was appointed on the spot Administrator of Southern Zhao Commandery; because of his love of wine he achieved no administrative merit.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongan he was appointed on the spot administrator of Southern Zhao Commandery. His love of wine left him no record of merit.

literal: When Luoyang collapsed and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement, Yuanzhong abandoned his office and returned home, secretly planning a righteous rising.
idiomatic: When Luoyang fell and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement, Yuanzhong abandoned his office and returned home, secretly planning a righteous rising.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor led his host eastward, he went of his own accord to welcome him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan led his host eastward, Yuanzhong went of his own accord to welcome him.

literal: He rode an open carriage, bearing a plain zither and unstrained wine to see the Grand Ancestor; he thereupon advanced strategies of alliance and opposition, declaring his loyalty in full, and won deep favor and acceptance.
idiomatic: He rode an open carriage, bearing a plain zither and a jar of unstrained wine to see Gao Huan. He thereupon laid out stratagems of alliance and opposition, declared his loyalty in full, and won deep favor.

literal: At the time Governor Erzhu Yusheng held the province with rebellious troops; Yuanzhong first gathered a force on Western Mountain, then joined the main army, captured and executed Yusheng.
idiomatic: At the time Governor Erzhu Yusheng held the province with rebellious troops. Yuanzhong first gathered a force on Western Mountain, then joined the main army, captured Yusheng, and executed him.

literal: He was immediately ordered to provisionally administer Yin Province affairs.
idiomatic: He was immediately ordered to provisionally administer Yin Province.

literal: At the beginning of the restoration he was appointed General of the Central Army and Minister Steward.
idiomatic: At the beginning of the restoration he was appointed general of the central army and minister steward.

literal: In the second year he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonial and Great Arbiter of Yin Province.
idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to minister of ceremonial and great arbiter of Yin Province.

literal: Later, because his older cousin Jin was senior in years, he yielded the arbiter's post to him.
idiomatic: Later, because his older cousin Jin was senior in years, he yielded the arbiter's post to him.

literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made general who pacifies the south.

literal: When Emperor Wu was about to take an empress — the Grand Ancestor's eldest daughter — he ordered Yuanzhong and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo to conduct the betrothal mission to Jinyang.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojuan was about to take an empress — Gao Huan's eldest daughter — he ordered Yuanzhong and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo to conduct the betrothal mission to Jinyang.

literal: At every feast the Grand Ancestor would recount old affairs, then clap his hands and laugh with delight, saying, "This man drove me to raise the banner.
idiomatic: At every feast Gao Huan would recount old affairs, then clap his hands and laugh with delight. "This man drove me to raise the banner,

literal: " He was granted one white horse.
idiomatic: " he would say, and grant him one white horse.

literal: Yuanzhong joked to the Grand Ancestor, "If you do not make me palace attendant, I shall find another place to raise the banner.
idiomatic: Yuanzhong joked to Gao Huan, "If you do not make me palace attendant, I shall find another place to raise the banner.

literal: " The Grand Ancestor replied, "Places to raise the banner are not lacking — I only fear that an old man like this cannot be encountered again.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan replied, "Places to raise the banner are not lacking — I only fear that an old man like this cannot be encountered again.

literal: " Yuanzhong said, "It is precisely because this old man is hard to meet that I do not leave.
idiomatic: " Yuanzhong said, "It is precisely because this old man is hard to meet that I do not leave.

literal: " Thereupon he seized the Grand Ancestor's beard and laughed loudly.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he seized Gao Huan's beard and laughed loudly.

literal: The Grand Ancestor also fully grasped his refined intent and valued him deeply.
idiomatic: Gao Huan also fully grasped his refined intent and valued him deeply.

literal: Later, when the Grand Ancestor escorted the empress and was hunting at Jin Marsh, Yuanzhong's horse fell and injured him; he collapsed on the spot and only revived after a long time.
idiomatic: Later, when Gao Huan escorted the empress and was hunting at Jin Marsh, Yuanzhong's horse fell and injured him. He collapsed on the spot and only revived after a long time.

literal: The Grand Ancestor personally tended to him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan personally tended to him.

literal: That year he was enfeoffed Baron of Jinyang County with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: That year he was enfeoffed baron of Jinyang County with a fief of five hundred households.

literal: Later for a minor offense he lost his office.
idiomatic: Later, for a minor offense, he lost his office.

literal: At the time the court was divided, and those of the righteous banner were often suspected and obstructed.
idiomatic: At the time the court was divided, and men of the righteous banner were often suspected and obstructed.

literal: Husi Chun and the rest, because Yuanzhong was indifferent to glory and profit and did not concern himself with worldly affairs, did not place him among those they envied and resented.
idiomatic: Husi Chun and the rest, because Yuanzhong was indifferent to glory and profit and did not concern himself with worldly affairs, did not count him among those they envied and resented.

literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made director of the secretariat.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was again made Minister of Ceremonial.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was again made minister of ceremonial.

literal: Later he was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry.
idiomatic: Later he was additionally made general of agile cavalry.

literal: In the fourth year he was appointed bearer of the staff and Governor of Guang Province.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed bearer of the staff and governor of Guang Province.

literal: At the time the province was stricken by disaster and famine; the people were gaunt with hunger. Yuanzhong memorialized asking for relief grain, to be recovered through autumn collection.
idiomatic: At the time the province was stricken by disaster and famine; the people were gaunt with hunger. Yuanzhong memorialized asking for relief grain, to be recovered through autumn collection.

literal: In reply he was permitted ten thousand shi.
idiomatic: In reply he was permitted ten thousand shi.

literal: Yuanzhong judged that ten thousand shi distributed among the people would amount to no more than a sheng or dou per household — empty reputation that would not relieve their distress — and so released one hundred fifty thousand shi to relieve them.
idiomatic: Yuanzhong judged that ten thousand shi spread among the people would amount to no more than a sheng or dou per household — empty reputation that would not relieve their distress. He released one hundred fifty thousand shi to relieve them.

literal: When the matter was finished he memorialized the facts; the court praised him and did not charge him.
idiomatic: When the matter was finished he memorialized the facts. The court praised him and did not charge him.

literal: At the end of Xinghe he was appointed palace attendant.
idiomatic: At the end of Xinghe he was appointed palace attendant.

literal: Though Yuanzhong held important posts, he never let official business weigh on his mind; he amused himself only with music and wine, was for the most part constantly drunk, and paid no attention at all to domestic affairs great or small.
idiomatic: Though Yuanzhong held important posts, he never let official business weigh on his mind. He amused himself only with music and wine, was for the most part constantly drunk, and paid no attention at all to domestic affairs great or small.

literal: Within his garden he planted fruit and medicinal herbs in abundance; when kinsmen and friends came to call, he always detained them for feasting and pleasure.
idiomatic: Within his garden he planted fruit and medicinal herbs in abundance. When kinsmen and friends came to call, he always detained them for feasting and pleasure.

literal: He would carry his slingshot and wine flask and roam through the lanes at leisure; whenever he met company for drinking, he was tranquil and at ease.
idiomatic: He would carry his slingshot and wine flask and roam through the lanes at leisure. Whenever he met company for drinking, he was tranquil and at ease.

literal: He often spread word among those in charge, saying, "My years approach twilight, my will and strength have declined; I have long held a distinguished office, blocking the path for the able.
idiomatic: He often spread word among those in charge, saying, "My years approach twilight, my will and strength have declined. I have long held a distinguished office, blocking the path for the able.

literal: If the court's generous grace will not yet release me, I beg an idle, secondary post in which to spend my remaining years.
idiomatic: If the court's generous grace will not yet release me, I beg an idle, secondary post in which to spend my remaining years.

literal: " In Wuding year one he was appointed Governor of Eastern Xu Province but firmly declined and did not accept.
idiomatic: " In Wuding year one he was appointed governor of Eastern Xu Province but firmly declined and did not accept.

literal: He was then made General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: He was then made general of agile cavalry and equal in protocol to three imperators.

literal: Once he presented Shizong with a tray of grapes.
idiomatic: Once he presented Gao Cheng with a tray of grapes.

literal: Shizong replied with one hundred bolts of fine silk and sent him a letter saying, "Your rank as Equal in Protocol stands next to the pillars of state; your mind is steadfast and plain; you have served both in the provinces and at court in posts of weight and consequence.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng replied with one hundred bolts of fine silk and sent him a letter saying, "Your rank as equal in protocol stands next to the pillars of state. Your mind is steadfast and plain. You have served both in the provinces and at court in posts of weight and consequence.

literal: Yet your house holds not a single stone's measure, your rooms are as empty as a suspended bell — surely it is because you hold wealth lightly and honor righteousness, serving the age and cherishing yourself.
idiomatic: Yet your house holds not a single stone's measure, your rooms are as empty as a suspended bell — surely it is because you hold wealth lightly and honor righteousness, serving the age and cherishing yourself.

literal: I have long admired you, my praise knows no limit; I have always wished to mark my esteem, but found no occasion.
idiomatic: I have long admired you, my praise knows no limit. I have always wished to mark my esteem, but found no occasion.

literal: Now your gift of grapes comes as a surprise — I am deeply touched.
idiomatic: Now your gift of grapes comes as a surprise — I am deeply touched.

literal: I send one hundred bolts of silk in token of your pure virtue.
idiomatic: I send one hundred bolts of silk in token of your pure virtue.

literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.
idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

literal: Sun Teng and Sima Ziru once went together to visit Yuanzhong; they found him sitting beneath a tree, wrapped in a quilt facing a wine jar, the courtyard overgrown and deserted.
idiomatic: Sun Teng and Sima Ziru once went together to visit Yuanzhong. They found him sitting beneath a tree, wrapped in a quilt facing a wine jar, the courtyard overgrown and deserted.

literal: He said to the two lords, "I never thought to find myself spreading coarse greens for guests today.
idiomatic: He said to the two lords, "I never thought to find myself spreading coarse greens for guests today.

literal: " He called his wife out; her clothes did not even reach the ground.
idiomatic: " He called his wife out; her clothes did not even reach the ground.

literal: The two exchanged glances, sighed, and departed; they sent generous gifts of grain, silk, and clothing, which Yuanzhong accepted and distributed.
idiomatic: The two exchanged glances, sighed, and departed. They sent generous gifts of grain, silk, and clothing, which Yuanzhong accepted and distributed.

literal: In the third year he again held his former office concurrently with Minister Steward.
idiomatic: In the third year he again held his former office concurrently with minister steward.

literal: That year he died in office. He was sixty.
idiomatic: That year he died in office. He was sixty.

literal: An edict posthumously granted five hundred bolts of silk and cloth, bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ji, Yin, and You, grand general, Duke over the Masses, and Governor of Ding Province, with posthumous title Jinghui.
idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted five hundred bolts of silk and cloth, bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ji, Yin, and You, grand general, duke over the masses, and governor of Ding Province, with the posthumous title Jinghui.

literal: At first, when Yuanzhong was about to enter office, he dreamed he held a torch and entered his father's tomb; he woke in the middle of the night in alarm and took it as a bad omen.
idiomatic: At first, when Yuanzhong was about to enter office, he dreamed he held a torch and entered his father's tomb. He woke in the middle of the night in alarm and took it as a bad omen.

literal: At dawn he told his teacher, who divined: "Great fortune — this means light shining upon your ancestors; you will in the end reach honor and eminence.
idiomatic: At dawn he told his teacher, who divined: "Great fortune — this means light shining upon your ancestors. You will in the end reach honor and eminence.

literal: " His son Sao inherited.
idiomatic: " His son Sao inherited.

literal: Sao, styled Dekuang, was clever and perceptive in youth, talented in the arts; music, board games, and the like — he mastered many.
idiomatic: Sao, styled Dekuang, was clever and perceptive in youth and talented in the arts. Music, board games, and the like — he mastered many.

literal: He once gathered various tones and separately devised an instrument called the Eight Strings; men of the age praised his inventive mind.
idiomatic: He once gathered various tones and separately devised an instrument called the Eight Strings. Men of the age praised his inventive mind.

literal: He first entered service as itinerant staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: He first entered service as itinerant staff officer in the ministry of works.

literal: He rose through offices to Administrator of Henei, where the common people found peace under him.
idiomatic: He rose through offices to administrator of Henei, where the common people found peace under him.

literal: He entered court as secretary in the Ministry of Rites of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He entered court as secretary in the ministry of rites of the masters of writing.

literal: He died in the eighth year of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Tianbao.

literal: Yuanzhong's younger clansman Mi, styled Xiyong, was a native of Pingji.
idiomatic: Yuanzhong's younger clansman Mi, styled Xiyong, came from Pingji.

literal: His grandfather Boying was Administrator of Dong Commandery in Wei, posthumously granted Governor of You Province.
idiomatic: His grandfather Boying was administrator of Dong Commandery in Wei, posthumously granted governor of You Province.

literal: His father Huan was supervising secretary of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Henei, posthumously granted Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: His father Huan was supervising secretary of the masters of writing, administrator of Henei, posthumously granted governor of Qing Province.

literal: Mi in youth had integrity of character; when Erzhu Zhao committed regicide, he secretly joined with leading men and with Gao Ang of Bohai to plan vengeance.
idiomatic: Mi in youth had integrity of character. When Erzhu Zhao committed regicide, he secretly joined with leading men and with Gao Ang of Bohai to plan vengeance.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor came out of Shandong, Mi followed the righteous rising with troops; he was remotely appointed Governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed Marquis of Rongcheng County with a fief of four hundred households.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan came out of Shandong, Mi followed the righteous rising with troops. He was remotely appointed governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed marquis of Rongcheng County with a fief of four hundred households.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao reached Guang'a, the Grand Ancestor ordered Mi to recruit five thousand troops from Yin and Ding provinces to garrison the Yellow Sand and Jingxing passes.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao reached Guang'a, Gao Huan ordered Mi to recruit five thousand troops from Yin and Ding provinces to garrison the Yellow Sand and Jingxing passes.

literal: When Zhao was defeated at Hanling and retreated to Jinyang, Mi followed the army to pacify Zhao.
idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated at Hanling and retreated to Jinyang, Mi followed the army to pacify him.

literal: The Grand Ancestor then had Xue Xunyi provisionally administer Bing Province affairs and appointed Mi Governor of Jian Province.
idiomatic: Gao Huan then had Xue Xunyi provisionally administer Bing Province and appointed Mi governor of Jian Province.

literal: He was additionally made Governor of Xiang Province.
idiomatic: He was additionally made governor of Xiang Province.

literal: For more than ten years in the province he thoroughly mastered the art of securing the borders; his authority and reputation were known beyond the frontier.
idiomatic: For more than ten years in the province he thoroughly mastered the art of securing the borders. His authority and reputation were known beyond the frontier.

literal: The Grand Ancestor repeatedly sent personal letters of comfort and inquiry, and also granted him provisions and horses.
idiomatic: Gao Huan repeatedly sent personal letters of comfort and inquiry, and also granted him provisions and horses.

literal: When Hou Jing rebelled abroad, he lured Mi into captivity and granted him office and rank.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled abroad, he lured Mi into captivity and granted him office and rank.

literal: When Jing was defeated and Mi returned to court, the court judged that Mi had followed Jing without genuine intent and did not punish him.
idiomatic: When Jing was defeated and Mi returned to court, the court judged that Mi had followed Jing without genuine intent and did not punish him.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for past merit he was appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and restored to his original marquisate of the county; he died.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, for past merit he was appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and restored to his original county marquisate; he died.

literal: Posthumously granted Palace Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted palace director of the masters of writing and governor of Ji Province.

literal: Mi's character was upright and direct, with proper conduct.
idiomatic: Mi's character was upright and direct, with proper conduct.

literal: Because his mother had been ill for years and famous physicians could not cure her, he thoroughly studied classical prescriptions until he mastered acupuncture and medicine, and his mother's illness was removed.
idiomatic: Because his mother had been ill for years and famous physicians could not cure her, he thoroughly studied classical prescriptions until he mastered acupuncture and medicine, and his mother's illness was removed.
